why: The frozen manifest pins ONE iteration's treatment and pool. When an iteration closes and its result forces a treatment change, the tree legitimately stops matching that pin — and until the next pool is mined there is nothing to freeze. Without a lifecycle that state is unrepresentable, so CI ends up asking a closed iteration's question of an unfrozen candidate. This record names which iteration, if any, is active.

states.frozen: an iteration is registered: its treatment and pool are pinned, the full freeze assertions are armed, and trajectories may run
states.between: no iteration is registered: the tree may differ from the last closed treatment, no freeze claim is made, development and mining are allowed and pilot execution is FORBIDDEN

transition: frozen -> closed -> between -> (mine a fresh pool) -> frozen. One-way: a closed iteration is never reopened and its pins never change. Only freeze-pilot-manifest.mjs --derive moves the protocol back to frozen.
